newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU to agree employment clause at summit - Van Mierlo.
newsitem.headline: EU to agree employment clause at summit - Van Mierlo.

text.p: Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo said on Monday he believed European Union members would agree on including a clause on unemployment in an EU reform treaty to be agreed in Amsterdam in June.

"I believe that we are getting a consensus on an employment paragraph. I am confident that it will be possible to get a convincing paragraph that will get the agreement of all," van Mierlo told reporters after a meeting with his German counterpart Klaus Kinkel.

The two men met in the north German port city of Hamburg to discuss preparations for Tuesday's council of EU foreign ministers and for the EU's reform summit in June, intended to agree a wide range of institutional reforms.

The EU's executive body, the European Commission, wants employment to be included in the Amsterdam Treaty as a key objective of the union. The Netherlands, as holder of the six-month rotating presidency, is entrusted with shepherding the talks to a successful conclusion.

Discussions have centred on a proposal put forward in a draft treaty by the Irish presidency last December which would commit member states to coordinate their employment policies and to set objectives to get people back to work.

There has been major opposition from Britain's Conservative government, although the Labour Party, which is favourite to win Thursday's general election, is more sympathetic to coordinating unemployment policy.

Van Mierlo told the news conference, conducted on a pleasure boat cruising around Hamburg's harbour, that Britain's Euro-sceptical stance had slowed progress towards agreement on EU reforms. But he cautioned against thinking agreement would be much easier if the Labour Party were in power.
"I have to say that the views of the Labour Party are not so simple with reference to the future of Europe," he said.
The two men also discussed relations with Iran, under strain since a Berlin court three weeks ago accused Tehran of ordering the murder of four Kurdish Iranian dissidents in Berlin in 1992.
Kinkel declined to comment on the issue ahead of the EU foreign ministers' meeting on Tuesday.

The EU has suspended a so-called "critical dialogue" with Tehran, and all members except Greece have withdrawn their ambassadors for consultations. However, EU diplomats in Brussels and Tehran said the ambassadors were likely to start returning as early as this week.
